hints: Write down the standard normal standardization formula $Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$.
Substitute $X = 0$ and $\mu = 1.5\sigma$ into the standardization expression to eliminate $\sigma$.
Find $\mathrm{P}(Z > -1.5) = \Phi(1.5)$ using the symmetry of the standard normal curve.
walkthrough:
Express the required probability in terms of $Z$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 0) = \mathrm{P}(Z > -1.5)$$

Use normal symmetry and read from the standard normal table:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > -1.5) = \Phi(1.5)$$
$$\Phi(1.5) \approx 0.9332 \approx 0.933$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Write down the given distribution parameters.
We are given $X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ where $\mu = 1.5\sigma$.
We wish to calculate $\mathrm{P}(X > 0)$.

Step 2: Standardize the boundary $X = 0$:
$$Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $X = 0$ and $\mu = 1.5\sigma$:
$$z = \frac{0 - 1.5\sigma}{\sigma} = \frac{-1.5\sigma}{\sigma} = -1.5$$

Step 4: Use the symmetry of the standard normal distribution:
By reflection symmetry across $Z = 0$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > -1.5) = \mathrm{P}(Z < 1.5) = \Phi(1.5)$$

Step 5: Look up $\Phi(1.50)$ in the normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(1.50) = 0.9332 \approx 0.933$$

hints: Translate '87.5% last longer than 70 hours' into $\mathrm{P}(Y > 70) = 0.875$, so $\mathrm{P}(Y < 70) = 0.125$.
Find the $z$-value corresponding to an upper tail of $0.875$, which has a negative sign because 70 is below the mean of 120.
Set up the standardization equation $\dfrac{70 - 120}{s} = -z$ and solve for $s$.
walkthrough:
Translate the battery life distribution statement into a probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y > 70) = 0.875 \implies \mathrm{P}(Y < 70) = 1 - 0.875 = 0.125$$

Find the standard normal $z$-value corresponding to this lower tail:
$$\Phi(z) = 0.875 \implies z \approx 1.151$$
$$\text{Since } 70 < \mu, \quad Z = -1.151$$

Set up the standardization equation with $\mu = 120$ and solve for $s$:
$$\frac{70 - 120}{s} = -1.151$$
$$\frac{-50}{s} = -1.151 \implies s = \frac{50}{1.151} \approx 43.4\text{ hours} \quad (\text{or } 43.5)$$

ai_rubric.Finding Normal Distribution Parameters: Sets up (70 - 120)/s = -1.151 and solves for s = 43.4 or 43.5.

teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: State the model and the given probability.
Let battery life be $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(120, s^2)$.
We are given that $87.5\%$ of batteries last longer than $70$ hours:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y > 70) = 0.875$$

Step 2: Convert to the cumulative probability below $70$:
$$\mathrm{P}(Y < 70) = 1 - 0.875 = 0.125$$

Step 3: Determine the standardized $z$-value.
Because $70$ is below the mean $\mu = 120$, the standardized score must be negative:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z < z_0) = 0.125 \implies \Phi(-z_0) = 1 - 0.125 = 0.875$$

Look up $0.875$ in the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(1.15) = 0.8749, \quad \text{difference of } 1 \text{ gives } 2 \implies -z_0 \approx 1.151 \implies z_0 = -1.151$$

Step 4: Standardize and solve for $s$:
$$Z = \frac{Y - \mu}{s}$$
$$-1.151 = \frac{70 - 120}{s} = \frac{-50}{s}$$
$$s = \frac{-50}{-1.151} = \frac{50}{1.151} \approx 43.44 \approx 43.4\text{ hours}$$
(Using $z = 1.150$ gives $s \approx 43.5\text{ hours}$; both are accepted).
